BLOCKER: `core/packaging.py` gains new shipped validation logic (`validate_residency`, `residency_section`, `residency_path`) while AGENTS/EDP language rule mandates new shipped logic in Go; the diff self-grants an exemption by editing `config/language-rule.json`'s allowlist — a governed rule should not be relaxed inside the same change that violates it.

Fail-open on corrupt policy: `_policy()` prints "BLOCK policy unreadable" and returns `gate_mode: block` + `_error`, but `main()` never inspects `_error`; if the manifest is valid the gate exits 0. A compliance gate must hard-fail (exit 2) when its own policy source is unreadable.

Default test runs mutate tracked repo state: `test_gate_report_is_non_fatal` invokes the gate without `PF_RESIDENCY_EVENT`/`PF_RESIDENCY_JSONL`, so the test writes `engineering/residency-gate.json`/`.jsonl` into the working tree — CI/test side effects on a registered evidence artifact.
MAJOR: Frozen error-code contract broken: unknown home `XX` produces `RESIDENCY_PROFILE_UNREADABLE` (both Go `LoadProfile` and Python), never `RESIDENCY_UNKNOWN_HOME`; the code only fires for empty/regex-invalid homes. AC and the "frozen codes" doc are not honored, and conformance tests assert only booleans, not codes.

`kms.region` may be empty and still pass: Go checks it only `if m.KMS.Region != ""` and Python builds the region list as `[]` when unset; AC requires `kms {provider, region, rotation_days>0}` — a KMS-less-residency declaration validates clean.

Validation policy is duplicated in three places (Go `Validate`, Python `validate_residency`, Python gate `hard_prefix` tuple) with divergent semantics: Go invoked with `--mode warn` exits 0 on everything, while the Python gate independently re-decides which codes are "hard" — the "Go is the authority" claim is structurally false and drift is only detected at runtime as a WARN.

Runtime Python/Go verdict divergence only warns and continues (`Python/Go verdict divergence; Go is authoritative` then evaluates `go_valid` alone); AC5 demands identical pass/block — a divergent Python-invalid/Go-valid manifest silently ships. Divergence must block.

The structured evidence event is best-effort: `_event()` swallows all write/rotation failures to a stderr WARN without affecting exit code, so the AC-required bounded event can silently vanish while the gate reports success (observability gap).

`config/store-registry.json` registers `residency-gate.json`, `residency-gate.jsonl`, `products/*/residency-manifest.json` with `target.status: "exists"` though none exist at registration time; an evidence/config registry that pre-declares existence weakens drift detection.

`residency-policy.json` ownership is incoherent: registry owner is `go/backupdrill/region.go` (region cells) while docs assign the `gate_mode` rollout lever to "a recorded decision" — no single accountable owner for a security-relevant policy lever.
MINOR: Python `_load_json` has no size cap while Go enforces 64KB on manifest and profile — asymmetric DoS/robustness between the two paths.

Backup group can be "populated" with zero regions (`regions: []` + encrypted + frequency passes missing-group and subset checks in both validators), weakening the AC's `backup {regions, ...}` requirement.

Go `Manifest.Template` is retained but Python `residency_section` pops `template`/`notes` — the emitted packaging manifest and the Go-validated artifact are not the same document shape, complicating future parity.
`--mode warn` explicitly passed by a user is still silently escalated to block by the expiry check, overriding operator intent without a distinct exit/report signal.
`residency_path(scope, ...)` ignores `scope` entirely — dead parameter that will mislead future callers; also `PF_RESIDENCY_PROFILES` env indirection is undocumented in RESIDENCY-MANIFEST-GATE.md.

No test updates for `language-rule` allowlist or precheck gate-count assertions (AC requires language_rule_review + precheck 45+ gates coverage); existing tests asserting exact allowlist contents may now fail.
`go run` compiles the validator on every gate invocation in the "fast" CI tier (120s timeout) — build a vetted binary once and cache, or the gate becomes a flaky latency source.
NIT: `test_packaging_residency.py` uses single blank lines between top-level functions (PEP8 E302) and an inline `import os` inside a test — inconsistent with repo style.
`_notes` key added to `config/language-rule.json` is schema pollution unless the checker explicitly tolerates unknown keys.
Gate prints its own WARN line in addition to Go's stderr WARN in warn mode — duplicated, slightly different summaries.
`--mode` values other than warn/block in `pfresidency` are treated as block implicitly; validate and reject explicitly.
Duplicate `RESIDENCY_HOME_NOT_ALLOWED` emission in Python (profile check and manifest check) inflates error lists.
SUMMARY: Solid scaffolding (Go module, fixtures, conformance harness, ownership registry entries), but the change weakens a governing language rule via a self-granted allowlist edit, fails open on unreadable policy, and ships a Python re-implementation of the policy engine that contradicts the "Go is authoritative" claim. The frozen error-code contract (notably RESIDENCY_UNKNOWN_HOME) and the kms.region requirement are not actually enforced. Recommend: move `validate_residency` to Go with Python as a thin reader, hard-fail on policy/validator unavailability, assert error codes (not booleans) in conformance tests, and isolate event writes behind temp paths in tests.
